findings.summary: FEC dismissed Campaign Legal Center complaint MUR 8090 against Save America 6-0 on 2024-06-06; held that BCRA soft-money ban was not violated by Save America's $60M transfer to MAGA Inc super PAC
findings.detail: Campaign Legal Center filed an FEC complaint in November 2022 alleging Trump and Save America violated BCRA's 'soft money' ban (52 USC 30125(e)) by transferring $60M to MAGA Inc — a sum vastly exceeding the $5,000 federal-candidate contribution limit to other PACs. CLC and NRDC Action Votes filed a supplemental/amended complaint in May 2023. The matter became MUR 8090. On 2024-06-06 the FEC voted 6-0 to dismiss, taking the position that a federal candidate or officeholder who merely transfers hard money from a leadership PAC to a soft-money entity does not trigger BCRA's soft-money ban, even if the recipient super PAC engages in activities 'in connection with' federal elections. The dismissal effectively legalized the funding pipeline now used to underwrite Trump's legal-defense apparatus. CLC also filed a separate complaint regarding 'concealing' legal-expense payments by reimbursing an accounting firm that fronted them, alleging corporate-contribution and reporting violations (status not confirmed via this wave).

findings.detail: Monthly Save America legal-fee disbursement totals (synthesis from 1,075 records classified as legal): pre-FBI-raid 2021-02 through 2022-07 averaged $10K-$200K (background civil work). 2022-08 (Mar-a-Lago FBI raid 8/8/22): jump to $3,908,797 — a 19x month-over-month spike driven by $3M one-time payment to Critton Luttier & Coleman trust account (2022-08-30) and onboarding of Boris Epshteyn / Continental PLLC. 2022-09 $1.56M; 2022-10 (Smith appointed 11/18) $1.78M; 2022-11 $3.19M; 2022-12 $3.25M. 2023 indictment year (Bragg 3/30, Smith SDFL 6/8, Smith DDC 8/1, Willis Fulton 8/14): monthly averages $4M+, peak 2023-07 $5.19M. 2024 (NY hush-money trial Apr-May, conviction 5/30, Cannon dismissal 7/15, Butler attempt 7/13, election 11/5): peak 2024-02 $6.24M, 2024-10 (final pre-election push) $5.14M. Cumulative 2024-cycle legal disbursements ~$45M+. After Trump's 2025-01-20 inauguration, monthly legal fees collapsed: 2025-01 $382K, 2025-02 $942K, 2025-03 $333K, 2025-05 only $22K — a 99% reduction from 2024 peaks consistent with DOJ dropping federal prosecutions and SDFL classified-docs case being final. Resumed in 2025-06 ($1.38M) and 2025-12 ($3.12M) for ongoing civil litigation (Carroll appeal, NY judgments, post-presidential civil cases) and tariff/IEEPA constitutional matters.

findings.summary: Save America made ZERO independent expenditures (Schedule E) across all four cycles 2020-2026; spending was channeled exclusively through transfers and operating disbursements (legal/consulting/payroll/travel)
findings.detail: FEC Schedule E query for committee_id C00762591 returned 0 records. Confirmed by FEC totals field 'independent_expenditures' = 0.00 in every cycle. Save America does NOT make independent expenditures itself — that role is reserved for the affiliated super PAC MAGA Inc (C00825851). Save America's spending is structured almost entirely as: (a) operating expenditures (legal services, consulting, vendor payments) — $159.3M total / 10,777 records on FEC line 'Other Federal Operating Expenditures'; (b) contributions to other federal committees $65.3M / 174 records; (c) transfers to affiliated party committees $21.6M / 53 records (all to Make America Great Again PAC C00580100); (d) other disbursements $7.06M / 52 records; (e) refunds to individuals $561K / 70 records.

findings.summary: Save America's individual-donor receipts collapsed from $1.18M (2022 cycle) to $129K (2024 cycle) to $12.8K (2026 cycle); after 2020-21 election-defense fundraising bait-and-switch, virtually all funds now arrive via inter-PAC transfers and the JFC waterfall
findings.detail: FEC committee totals show stark donor-base collapse for Save America: 2020 cycle (Oct-Dec 2020) — individual contributions $1,054,827.84; transfers from affiliated party $30,452,064.97 (the famous 'Election Defense Fund' funnel where ~60% of donations to the joint Trump/RNC fundraising effort went to Save America). 2022 cycle — individual $1,176,102.90; transfers from affiliated $108,035,602.57 (the residue of 2020 election-defense money + ongoing JFC flow). 2024 cycle — individual $129,285.05 (a 91% drop from 2022); transfers from affiliated $39,293,500.97 plus the $60M MAGA Inc refund. 2026 cycle YTD — individual $12,774.69 (a 90% further drop); transfers from affiliated $15,481,589.59 (essentially all funding). Confirmed FEC complaint history (multiple 2021-2022 actions) about 'Official Election Defense Fund' solicitations directing dollars meant for 2020 recount efforts to Save America's general fund. The arc establishes Save America as a structural pass-through for inter-committee Trump money, not a small-dollar grassroots PAC: 99.92% of 2026 funds are inter-committee transfers.

findings.detail: Beyond legal fees, Save America's spending shows distinct pattern phases. 2021-2022 (pre-indictment, post-presidency political infrastructure phase): $11.34M to EVENT STRATEGIES INC (VA — Trump rally production through 2024); $2.74M to PAYCHEX (in-house staff payroll — Save America has a payroll); $1.55M to FACEBOOK ads (terminated 2022-02 when Trump returned to Twitter); $2.44M to AMERICAN EXPRESS (corporate card with travel/expenses); $2.79M to TAKE BACK GEORGIA + $1.5M GET GEORGIA RIGHT PAC (2022 GA primary intervention); $1M each to CONSERVATIVE PARTNERSHIP INSTITUTE (Mark Meadows / Cleta Mitchell think tank — 2021-07-26), AMERICA FIRST POLICY INSTITUTE (post-presidency think tank — 2021-06-15), OUR AMERICAN CENTURY (2022-05-10), AMERICAN LEADERSHIP ACTION (2022-05-02); $650K to SMITHSONIAN INSTITUTION (2022-07-14 — official portrait commissions per public reporting); $650K to WYOMING VALUES (anti-Cheney 2022 primary super PAC); $450K Free and Fair Arizona Elections; $200K Arizona First Project + Michigan Works PACs; $150K RNC; $150K Article III Foundation (2024-02-01 — judicial advocacy). 2023-2024 (legal-defense phase): operational spending crowded out — Event Strategies stops in Feb 2024, Facebook is gone, only legal vendors and Red Curve/Paychex/AmEx remain. Notable post-2024-election spending: SULLIVAN & CROMWELL LLP $3.96M across just 4 records 2025-03 to 2025-12 (NY appellate work; first major non-Trump-personal-counsel firm to receive serious money). PRINTINGHOUSE PRESS LTD $835K 2024-09 to 2025-06 (election mailers / merchandise printer).
